AbstractText.Label: OBJECTIVE
AbstractText.content: To determine the effect of activity-based mirror therapy (MT) on motor recovery and gait in chronic poststroke hemiparetic subjects.

AbstractText.Label: PARTICIPANTS
AbstractText.content: Thirty-six chronic poststroke (15.89 ± 9.01 months) hemiparetic subjects (age: 46.44 ± 7.89 years, 30 men and functional ambulation classification of median level 3).

AbstractText.Label: INTERVENTIONS
AbstractText.content: Activity-based MT comprised movements such as ball-rolling, rocker-board, and pedalling. The activities were provided on the less-affected side in front of the mirror while hiding the affected limb. The movement of the less-affected lower limb was projected as over the affected limb. Conventional motor therapy based on neurophysiological approaches was also provided to the experimental group. The control group received only conventional management.

AbstractText.Label: MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES
AbstractText.content: Brunnstrom recovery stages (BRS), Fugl-Meyer assessment lower extremity (FMA-LE), Rivermead visual gait assessment (RVGA), and 10-metre walk test (10-MWT).

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: Postintervention, the experimental group exhibited significant and favourable changes for FMA-LE (mean difference = 3.29, 95% CI = 1.23-5.35, p = .003) and RVGA (mean difference = 5.41, 95% CI = 1.12-9.71, p = .015) in comparison to the control group. No considerable changes were observed on 10-MWT.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSIONS
AbstractText.content: Activity-based MT facilitates motor recovery of the lower limb as well as reduces gait deviations among chronic poststroke hemiparetic subjects.
